AiCustomerServiceCopilotKnowledgeWorkspa.description: The customer-service copilot's configuration for one scope (pack 10.1.10). A field left out takes its default, not its old value.

scopePath.description: **The partition key** (ADR-0005), and the upsert key: one row per scope.

dataSources.description: The authorised data the copilot may read, always within the asking agent's own permissions.

knowledgeCollectionIds.description: `ai.knowledge_collection` rows holding service procedures, product information, refund rules, ticket policies, venue instructions, FAQs and internal SOPs.

brandTone.description: Tone guidance applied to every draft.

autoSend.description: Channels where an approved automation may send without an agent. Empty means every customer-facing message waits for a person.

patternDetection.description: Flags a systemic problem when many cases share one cause.

AiCustomerServiceCopilotKnowledgeWorkspa.x-ticvai-persistence: none — projection over marketing.service_copilot_config (new), ai.policy and ai.knowledge_collection
AiCustomerServiceCopilotKnowledgeWorkspa.description: The stored configuration and what is in effect at that scope after the tenant row and the AI policy are applied.

effective.description: The narrowest of this row, its tenant row and `getAiPolicy`.

CallDisposition.description: BL-082. **A conversation could be closed and nothing recorded why it ended** — information, no sale, sale successful. **That is the measure a contact centre runs on**, and its absence makes every conversation look identical in a report.

callbackAt.description: **An agent could not schedule a callback with the case attached**, so a promise to ring back lived in somebody's notebook.

id.description: Created on the device (`CreateCaseRequest.id`, `raiseMyCase`), so a ULID.

caseNumber.description: **Server-assigned: the venue prefix plus a sequence per venue** (decided 28 September, audit R152). Not gapless; only tax invoices are gapless, per legal entity. Assigned when the case reaches the server, so a retry with the same `id` keeps its number.

guestName.description: **Resolved from `pii.subject` when the case is read, never stored on the case.** A name copied onto a case row is personal data outside the erasable store (ADR-0023), and it had no source anyway — no request carries it. Returned only to callers holding `GUEST_VIEW_PII`, as `searchGuests` does.

subject.description: **The case's one-line title**, not a person. Stored as `title` so the table does not hold `subject` beside `subject_id`; the wire keeps `subject` because screens bind it.

kind.description: What the guest said it was about, where the guest raised it.

channel.description: How the guest reached the venue — `CreateCaseRequest.channel`, or `inApp` for a case raised through `raiseMyCase`.

recordedAt.description: Device time the case was raised — the start of the SLA clock.

syncedAt.description: Server time the case arrived. Equal to `recordedAt` for a case raised online.

queueId.description: The `ServiceQueue` the case waits in, set by routing (`CaseRoutingRule.queueId`). Null once routed straight to an agent. (decided 29 September, data model for the agreed operations)

membershipId.description: The identity membership this case concerns (`identity.customer_membership`); member case notes are cases with this set. (decided 29 September, coordinator decision DM4, writers pass)

isSlaBreached.description: **Computed when read, never stored.** True once the case has been open longer than its SLA allows — the time from `recordedAt` to `resolvedAt` (or to now, while unresolved), less `slaPausedSeconds`, is past the target that set `slaDueAt`. A stored flag would need a job to flip it at the moment of breach, and no such job is designed; `listCases?breachedSla` filters on the same computation.

slaPausedSeconds.description: Accrued only while awaiting the guest. Waiting on an internal team does not pause the clock.

CaseKind.description:
**What the guest says the case is about**, in their words rather than the venue's taxonomy — `raiseMyCase` asks for it and `categoryId` is what staff file it under. Stored on the case, because a lost-property report that forgets it was one cannot be routed to the lost and found desk.
**`other` only with a note (decided 28 September, audit R222).** A case raised as `other` must carry a non-empty `detail` (`raiseMyCase`), or it is refused with 400; the notes are reviewed quarterly to add the real kinds they reveal.

Conversation.description: 22.8. **A conversation is not a case.** A case is a ticket measured in hours; a conversation is a live session measured in seconds, with somebody waiting. A conversation may create a case; it is not one.

telephony.description:
BL-083. **`ConversationChannel` included `voice` with nothing behind it** — the model anticipated telephony and stopped at the enum.
**Not an integration, a binding.** Genesys, Avaya, Amazon Connect, Teams and 3CX all do call control themselves; what the platform needs is the call bound to the guest and the case, so **an agent who answers already knows who is calling and what about.**

fromNumberMasked.description: **Masked, and it is still personal data.** A phone number identifies a person more reliably than a name does.

recordingRef.description: Held by the provider, referenced here. **Recording consent is jurisdictional and the platform does not assume it** — a reference with no consent record is a recording nobody may play.

assistSessionId.description:
BL-094. **`startKioskAssist` recorded a staff member helping a guest and `createCase` recorded a service interaction, and neither referenced the other** — so the traceability 2.13.20 asks for had no link to follow.
**The link is here rather than on the assist session**, because a case may span several assists and an assist belongs to at most one case.

subjectId.description: 22.8.3. Resolved from phone, email, membership number or a signed-in session. **A conversation with none of those stays anonymous rather than being guessed at.**

queuePosition.description: Place among the unclaimed conversations in `queueId`, from the live agent queue (audit R149). Null once claimed.

estimatedWaitSeconds.description: From the live agent queue — the conversations ahead divided across that queue's agents online now (audit R149). Null once claimed.

handoverSummary.description: **The assistant's own account of what the guest wants**, so an agent opens with context rather than reading a transcript while somebody waits.

sentiment.description: 22.8.16. **`escalating` is a routing signal**, not a report line.

intent.description: 22.8.13. What the guest appears to want, used for routing.

sender.description: **Resolved, never declared.** The assistant is labelled as one — a guest talking to a bot that presents as a person is a complaint waiting for the moment they find out.

aiInteractionId.description: Where the assistant sent it. **Links the message to its tokens and cost**, so a conversation's spend is attributable (CF-14).

ConversationState.description: **`withAssistant` and `queued` are different, and the second has a person waiting.** Merging them makes the service level unmeasurable, because time with a bot is not time in a queue.

GuestTimelineEvent.description: Board 1.5. **Facts, notes and predictions distinguished on the row.**

nature.description: **A prediction and a gate scan are both useful and only one happened.**

IntelligentRoutingSkillsAssignmentEngine.description: One case routing rule (pack 10.2.3). Empty match lists match everything; all non-empty lists must match.

queueId.description: The queue this rule routes into; null routes straight to an agent.

eventWithinHours.description: Event proximity - matches only when the case's event starts within this many hours.

requiredSkills.description: Skills an agent must hold (`AgentServiceProfile.skills`), e.g. `ticketing`, `refunds`.

requireLanguageMatch.description: Only agents who speak the customer's language are candidates.

maxUtilizationRate.description: Agents above this workload are skipped.

respectSlaCapability.description: Skip agents whose current queue would push the case past its SLA.

stickyOwnership.description: Prefer the agent who last handled the customer or the reopened case, if available.

fallbackQueueId.description: Where the case goes when no candidate agent is available.

IntelligentRoutingSkillsAssignmentEngine.description: A routing rule as stored, with how often it has matched.
IntelligentRoutingSkillsAssignmentEngine.x-ticvai-persistence: none — the marketing.case_routing_rule (new) row plus a count over marketing.case

KioskAssistSession.description: 2.1.25. A staff member acting on a kiosk session remotely. **The guest can always see it and always end it** — remote assistance a guest cannot see or stop is surveillance.

staffDisplayName.description: **Shown on the kiosk.** A guest being helped should know by whom.

actionsTaken.description: **Every action recorded as the staff member's**, not the kiosk's. A cashier completing a guest's checkout remotely is a staff action on a guest cart.

OrderBookingTicketServiceWorkspaceInput.x-ticvai-record-definition: Permitted Service Actions (one per executed action)
OrderBookingTicketServiceWorkspaceInput.description: One service action on an order, taken from a case. Only an `execute` stores a row.

caseId.description: Required with `execute`; the action is recorded on this case.

targetPerformanceId.description: For `reschedule` and `exchange`, the option chosen from the evaluation.

recipientSubjectId.description: For `transfer` and `changeName`, the new ticket holder.

downstreamOperation.description: The operation that performed it, e.g. `rescheduleOrder`.

OrderBookingTicketServiceWorkspaceView.x-ticvai-persistence: none — projection over orders.sales_order, orders.order_line, orders.payment, access.entitlement, marketing.case_service_action (new) and the policies each owning operation reads
OrderBookingTicketServiceWorkspaceView.description: The order as a service agent sees it, what may be done to it, and what was done.

order.description: The order number shown to the guest.

channel.description: The sales channel the order came through.

lastAction.description: The action just executed; null on `evaluate`.

ServiceQueue.description: **A customer-service queue** (e.g. `eventDaySupport`). Cases (`Case.queueId`), routing rules (`queueId`, `fallbackQueueId`) and agents (`AgentAvailability.queueIds`) name it; `listContact` and `listAgentWorkloadAvailability` report per queue. Maintained by `setServiceQueueDefinition`, read by `listServiceQueues` (decided 29 September, writers pass). (decided 29 September, data model for the agreed operations)

overflowWaitSeconds.description: The queue's overflow threshold; a case waiting longer marks the queue `critical`.
